newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Haughey paid 1.3 mln punts, Dublin tribunal told.
newsitem.headline: Haughey paid 1.3 mln punts, Dublin tribunal told.

text.p: A tribunal investigating payments to politicians was told on Monday that former prime minister Charles Haughey received payments totalling 1.3 million punts from businessman Bernard "Ben" Dunne.
Council for the tribunal Dennis McCullough said when the tribunal opened that the money was paid to Haughey between December 1987 and November 1991.

"The evidence which Mr. Dunne will give will be that between December 1987 and November 1991, he arranged for 1.3 million Irish pounds to be paid to the benefit of Mr. Charles J. Haughey," McCullough said.

It was the first time that the name of the former Fianna Fail leader has been publicly mentioned as a recipient of cash paid out by Dunne before he was dropped from the board of Dunnes Stores in 1993.

McCullough, outlining evidence that will be given in coming days, also detailed payments made to Michael Lowry, the Fine Gael member of parliament who resigned as transport minister last year when reports of the Dunne payments came to light.

McCullough told the tribunal that in addition to the refurbishment of Lowry's Tipperary home, which cost 395,000 pounds, Lowry also received substantial amounts of cash as payment because of the business relationship between Dunnes Stores and Lowry's Streamline Refrigeration firm.
McCullough said the sums totalled approximately 200,000 but were accounted for because of the business relationship between Dunnes Stores and Lowry's company.
"Mr. Dunne sought no political favours and none was either offered or given," McCullough told the tribunal.
He said the refurbishment of Lowry's home, which Lowry has acknowledged, included furniture, paintings and "a custom-built double bed".
The tribunal is expected to call Dunne as its first witness later on Monday.
